why_the_guard_refuses: xhci_residue_page() classifies every PMM-unavailable frame (avail=0) as 3 'protected'; residue::claim() maps Protected to UNINSPECTED and returns not-readable; xhci_residue_read64() permits reads only inside frames in the guard's own reservation registry. Since C3a.2, OVMF ring pages are avail=0 (EFI-excluded), so they are indistinguishable from e820-reserved or non-RAM memory and the guard refuses (correctly, fail closed).

mapping_audit.existing_alias: phys [0, 1 GiB) is permanently mapped at KERNEL_VMA + phys since boot; kmap_init rebuilds it with W^X: 4 KiB pages over the kernel image, 2 MiB pages elsewhere with PDE_RW_2M = P|W|PS|NX, PAT index 0 (write-back). Every excluded firmware page below 1 GiB therefore already has exactly one mapping: this writable, non-executable, write-back alias. It predates C3a.3 and is the same path the C3a guard and pmm_alloc_frame use.
mapping_audit.devmap: devmap_map/devmap_scope refuse any range intersecting RAM or unknown map entries (DEVMAP_ERAM) and map device memory UC/WC only; the scope lease allocates its page table from the PMM and frees it on release. A RAM mapping through devmap is forbidden by design (cache-attribute aliasing).
mapping_audit.new_mapping_option: a separate read-only mapping of the firmware pages would need either a new page table (a PMM allocation, which the milestone forbids) or a RAM mapping through devmap (forbidden, and a UC alias of WB RAM is a coherency hazard). It would add a second alias instead of removing one.
mapping_audit.cache: the alias is write-back; firmware wrote the structures through the CPU and the halted controller through snooped DMA (coherent on QEMU; on x86 platforms DMA is snooped unless a device uses no-snoop TLPs, not covered here)

decision: GO with no new mapping: read-only inspection uses the existing permanent alias through the guard's existing 8-byte volatile loads, gated by a new frame class 'excluded firmware RAM' that requires (1) a page-aligned frame in [1 MiB, 1 GiB), (2) PMM avail=0 and alloc=0, (3) a boot reservation entry created by the C3a.2 EFI exclusion, and (4) an independent Rust re-derivation from the EFI map that the whole frame is tag-6 RAM touching no non-available entry and is EFI-excluded. Anything else stays 'protected/uninspected'. No PMM, page-table, devmap or device state changes; no release path.
